Some XBRL values are clearly mis-tagged (e.g. Southern First Bancshares $181.2m, The Bancorp $1.99bn) and were not used. Dallas and Minneapolis: no filing found that names the Reserve Bank and gives an amount. No FOIA release of a 'Capital Stock Master Report' for any Reserve Bank other than New York was found. auditors_unavailable.CUW: Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten. Searched for CBCS annual reports and financial statements and read the bank's own 'Condensed financial statements as of December 31, 2020' page at exch.centralbank.cw: it sets out the accounting principles used and names no external auditor, no audit firm, no auditor's report, no city and no report date. Press coverage of the 2022, 2023 and 2024 annual reports gave profit figures but no auditor. No readable source names the auditor.
auditors_unavailable.AND: Andorra has no central bank; it uses the euro under a monetary agreement with the EU and its financial supervisor is the Andorran Financial Authority (AFA), not a central bank. No central bank financial statements or external auditor exists to record.
auditors_unavailable.MCO: Monaco has no central bank; it uses the euro under a monetary agreement with the EU and banking supervision is carried out by French authorities. No central bank financial statements or external auditor exists to record.
auditors_unavailable.SMR: Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino. Two searches for the bank's bilancio and its relazione della societa di revisione returned only the accounts of San Marino's commercial banks (Banca Agricola Commerciale, Banca di San Marino) and pages of the Consiglio Grande e Generale; no BCSM financial statements or audit report page from bcsm.sm surfaced and nothing read named the central bank's external auditor.
auditors_unavailable.LIE: Liechtenstein has no central bank; it uses the Swiss franc under its currency treaty with Switzerland and supervision sits with the Financial Market Authority (FMA). No central bank financial statements or external auditor exists to record.
auditors_unavailable.KHM: National Bank of Cambodia. Read the NBC Annual Report 2022 (English) hosted on Open Development Cambodia at offset: the document, 200,796 characters of extracted text, covers 2022 operations, the banking system, payment systems, the 2023 outlook and statistical appendices, and carries no independent auditor's report and no auditor's signature block. Searches for separately published NBC audited financial statements returned only Cambodian commercial banks' reports. No readable source names the auditor.
auditors_unavailable.LAO: Bank of the Lao PDR. Searched for BOL annual reports and financial statements with an independent auditor's report; every result returned was a Lao commercial bank (BCEL, JDB, BFL-BRED, Booyoung, ICBC Vientiane, Maybank Laos), not the central bank. No BOL financial statements or auditor's report was found to read. No readable source names the auditor.
auditors_unavailable.BRN: Brunei Darussalam Central Bank. Read two BDCB publication PDFs under cms.bdcb.gov.bn. The BDCB Annual Report 2025 (publication 17824568929284490.pdf, 308,182 characters of extracted text) lists 'Independent Auditor's Report' at pages FS 5 to FS 9 in its contents, but those pages carry no extractable text: the document jumps from the Report of the Board (FS 1 to FS 4) straight to the Statement of Financial Position (FS 10), with the notes to the consolidated financial statements following to FS 52. Reads at offsets 0, 170000 and 200000 all confirmed the gap. A second BDCB PDF (17758095948258330.pdf, 66,915 characters) contains only Financial Intelligence Unit material and no auditor's report. The firm name is present only as an image, so no readable source names it.
auditors_unavailable.TKM: Central Bank of Turkmenistan. No search was able to surface any Central Bank of Turkmenistan annual report, financial statements or auditor's report; the bank publishes no audited accounts that search returned, and no statute text naming an external auditor was found. No readable source names the auditor.
auditors_unavailable.BLR: National Bank of the Republic of Belarus. Searched for NBRB annual reports and audited financial statements with an independent auditor's report; every result returned was a Belarusian commercial bank (Paritetbank, Belveb, RRB, MTBank, TC Bank) or an unrelated IMF country report. No NBRB auditor's report page was found to read and nothing named the audit organisation. No readable source names the auditor.
auditors_unavailable.OTHERS_NOT_REACHED: Not attempted this round - the ~25 WebFetch cap was spent on offset re-reads of already-identified documents: CUB, VEN, CUW, TKM, TUN, DZA, LBN, SYR, YEM, LBY, SDN, BDI, COD, COG, CPV, ERI, ETH, MRT, RWA, STP, TCD, BTN, LAO, MMR, JAM. case_updates.summary_addition: Olteanu was convicted of influence peddling and the Bucharest Court of Appeal set a final five-year sentence in October 2020, but on 31 March 2023 the same court confirmed that the case was closed as time-barred and his conviction annulled, while ordering confiscation of the €1 million.
case_updates.source_title: Agerpres, 'Bogdan Olteanu scapă definitiv de condamnare pe motiv că faptele s-au prescris' (31 Mar 2023)

case_updates.summary_addition: Simić was arrested on 11 January 2006 with Vladimir Zagrađanin, an investigation was ordered, and the NBS Council removed him as vice-governor on 16 January 2006; no indictment, verdict or acquittal was found.
case_updates.source_title: Central Banking, 'Serbian central bank deputy fired' (17 Jan 2006); Vreme (18 Jan 2006)

case_updates.summary_addition: No court outcome for the 2006 abuse-of-office charges against Mullei was found in the sources opened.
case_updates.source_title: Central Banking, 'CBK governor charged with abuse of office'

case_updates.summary_addition: On 26 April 2006 Judge Esenjan Abylkasymov acquitted Sarbanov and four other former finance officials, ruling there was no crime because they 'acted in the interests of state'; the prosecutor's office said it would appeal, and no appeal outcome was found.
case_updates.source_title: Central Banking, 'Kyrgyz's Sarbanov acted in interests of state' (28 Apr 2006)

case_updates.summary_addition: On 29 December 2002 Turkmenistan's Supreme Court sentenced Orazov in absentia to 25 years over alleged involvement in the 25 November 2002 armed attack on President Niyazov, and the People's Council raised it to life imprisonment the next day; Amnesty International called the trial grossly unfair. This conviction is for the alleged attack, not the loan-embezzlement accusation.

On 22 February 2017 prosecutors indicted 18 people in the Corpbank case, including former deputy governors Tsvetan Gounev and Roumen Simeonov for malfeasance in office over failing to exercise control over Corpbank; no verdict was found.
case_updates.source_title: BTA, '18 Persons Charged in Corpbank Case' (22 Feb 2017)

case_updates.summary_addition: The Milan Court of Appeal cut Fazio's Antonveneta sentence from four years to two years and six months on 28 May 2012, and on 28 November 2012 the Court of Cassation (judgment no. 12989, filed 21 March 2013) upheld the appeal ruling, making the conviction final.
case_updates.source_title: FISAC-CGIL, 'Confermata la condanna di Fazio'; Diritto Penale Contemporaneo on Cass. sez. II n. 12989/2013

case_updates.summary_addition: Around 30 January 2025 Ghana's Attorney-General filed notice to withdraw all charges against Asiama in both the uniBank and UT Bank trials; on 22 July 2025 the A-G also filed a nolle prosequi ending the uniBank case against Duffuor and others after recovering over 60% of the funds allegedly lost.
case_updates.source_title: Graphic Online, 'Attorney-General withdraws charges against former Deputy BoG Governor Johnson Asiama' (30 Jan 2025)

case_updates.summary_addition: At the Moscow City Court on 17 April 2007 prosecutors asked for 15 years in a strict-regime colony for Mishin, plus a fraud conviction over an apartment, and 12 years for tax official Oleg Alekseev; the verdict was not found.
No court outcome for the 2012 arrest warrant was found; Shabibi died on 8 January 2022, when the Central Bank of Iraq issued a statement mourning him as a distinguished former governor.
case_updates.source_title: Central Bank of Iraq news release (8 Jan 2022)

case_updates.summary_addition: As of 21 October 2026 the full Sejm vote on bringing Glapiński before the State Tribunal had not taken place; the Sejm Marshal said it would be taken up in the second half of November 2026 (sittings set for 5-6 and 17-19 November).
case_updates.source_title: Super Biznes, 'Trybunał Stanu dla prezesa NBP? Wiemy, kiedy kluczowe głosowanie' (21 Oct 2026)

case_updates.summary_addition: On 13 March 2024 the Hungarian government sent the draft amendment to the central bank act back for further consultation instead of submitting it to parliament, setting it aside 'at least for now'; a separate 2025 amendment package was proposed, and whether it passed was not checked.
case_updates.source_title: Telex, 'A kormány visszadobta a törvény módosítását...' (14 Mar 2024)
